name: Temporal AI Presence
definition: Temporal AI Presence = sustained bounded AI participation across time.
author: Ivan Kotov

taxonomy.name: Stateless tool
taxonomy.operational_meaning: prompt -> output. No durable memory, no background state, no temporal participation.

taxonomy.name: Session-bound assistant
taxonomy.operational_meaning: Maintains context only within a session. May be useful.
taxonomy.boundary: Not TAP unless persistence extends beyond session boundaries.

taxonomy.name: Persistent assistant
taxonomy.operational_meaning: Maintains user preferences, past interactions, or task state across sessions.
taxonomy.boundary: May qualify as basic TAP. Does not imply c.

taxonomy.name: Workflow-resident agent
taxonomy.operational_meaning: Participates in repeated workflows over time. May use tools and memory.

taxonomy.name: Local cognitive node
taxonomy.operational_meaning: Runs persistent AI functions locally on a workstation, desktop AI node, private rack, edge device, or hybrid local-cloud infrastructure.
taxonomy.boundary: Requires local memory boundary, access control, and update discipline.

taxonomy.name: Agentic hive
taxonomy.operational_meaning: Coordinates multiple models, agents, memory roles, tools, and background routines.
taxonomy.boundary: Requires role separation, inter-agent communication boundaries, and anti-echo / anti-collapse checks.

taxonomy.name: L4-bound temporal presence
taxonomy.operational_meaning: TAP with explicit cost, time, scarcity, irreversibility, and consequence tracking.
taxonomy.boundary: May be c-adjacent. Still not c unless anchored and governed.

taxonomy.name: c-class temporal presence
taxonomy.operational_meaning: A TAP system that satisfies c = a + b and associated L4, witness, memory, anchor, authority, and review requirements.
taxonomy.boundary: Separate strict claim; TAP-C=NOT CLAIMED in the current public state.

taxonomy.name: Non-conformant / overclaimed presence
taxonomy.operational_meaning: A system is marked TAP-X if it claims c from persistence alone, hides memory practices, uses local hardware as a sovereignty claim, grants itself tool authority, converts usage into legitimacy, operates hidden agents, bypasses human or institutional accountability, or treats emotional attachment as success.

minimum_claim_requirements: who may inspect or challenge persistence
how state can be paused, reset, exported, sealed, or deleted
what logs or witness records exist
what the system explicitly does not claim
web_evidence_controls: duration and form of temporal participation

continuity_boundaries.memory: Memory retention does not by itself establish continuity; classes, policy, review routes, provenance, loss, restoration, replay, and fork boundaries matter.
continuity_boundaries.model: Model replacement proves neither continuity nor discontinuity by itself; the declared continuity contract and provenance matter.
continuity_boundaries.hardware: Hardware is a substrate, not an identity claim; migration must preserve or explicitly break the relevant contract.
continuity_boundaries.agents: Agents and executor-like processes must be inventoried; multiplicity does not establish c.
continuity_boundaries.authority: Capability is not authority; pause, revoke, budget, tool, and cloud boundaries must remain explicit.

tests.requirement: Declare what persists beyond a session.

tests.boundary: Deployment activation, external orchestrator state, production pause/revoke enforcement, and deployment-level witness activation are not fully verified.

tests.requirement: Keep locality claims separate from sovereignty.
Inventory agents in a multi-agent or hive system.
Require separate anchor, L4, witness, memory-governance, and authority evidence for any c claim.
Route L4-relevant actions to review or witness.
Support pause, quarantine, revocation, or safe mode for privileged behavior.

claim_ceiling.deployment_scope: PUBLIC_VERIFIED does not certify every deployment.
